messages:
maria: FYI support is getting reports from Acme (tenant) — frequent 504/5xx and large p95 tails on hosted API since ~09:15 UTC. Symptoms: repeated client retries, billing auth failures in logs. Repro steps attached.

ops-bot: [alert] hosted.gateway.request-5xx spike: +220% p95 tail latency. Alert ID: AG-8350

alex: I'm on it. Can you post a recent request-id and sample trace?

maria: req_id: r-20260318-4f1a, customer says sequence of 6 concurrent requests triggered 504s. Logs:
```
2026-03-18T09:16:02Z ERROR request r-20260318-4f1a backend=hosted-gateway code=504 queue_depth=128 batcher_wait_ms=2350 auth=token-expired billing=rate-limited
```

Repro curl (note we hit timeout):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <RED>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","prompt":"hi"}' --max-time 20
```

raj: That queue_depth=128 is suspicious — continuous-batcher default cap is 128. Can we confirm if batcher heartbeat/flush patterns changed?

kevin: We deployed batcher/kv-cache heartbeat tweak at 2026-03-18T08:55 UTC (deploy id: deploy-20260318-055) that adjusted flush window for longseqs. Rolling back to previous release might be fastest mitigation.

alex: Rollback started. ops-bot, track deploy.

ops-bot: [deploy] rollback deploy-20260318-055 -> deploy-20260318-045 started by alex.

sophia: Customer is also seeing auth errors: billing service returns 429 for metering calls which makes runtime retry auth flow and blocks token refresh workers — could amplify queueing. Thoughts?

raj: Ah — token refresh worker queues are tied to same request queueing threadpool in hosted. If billing returns 429, refresh gets retried sync and holds batcher slots. Need a quick mitigation: decouple token refresh into separate low-priority executor or short-circuit on 429 for meter calls.

kevin: For immediate relief, I'm going to reduce continuous-batcher.max_queue_depth from 128 -> 80 on the affected pool and enable backpressure to drop oldest requests. That will shed load and buy time.

maria: Noted. Customer impact update: Acme reporting reduced 5xx after 09:35 UTC but still seeing sporadic 504s. They've asked for repro steps to validate fix.

alex: Steps to repro I used:
1) set concurrent requests N=6 with longseq=1024 tokens
2) force billing 429 by toggling test rate limiter on meter-service
3) run curl loop with small delay
Expectation: if queue saturates, p95 jumps and batcher_wait_ms > 2s and 504s appear.

raj: I'll add a temporary metric for token_refresh.block_time and batcher.queue_saturation to dashboard. Also adding a runbook note: If billing-side 429s correlate with queue spikes, treat as auth-metering feedback loop.

maria: Support messaging to customer: we identified a combination of batcher heartbeat change + billing 429 feedback loop that amplified queue depth. Rolling back and applying caps helped. We'll follow up with a permanent fix.

kevin: Post-rollback telemetry: queue_depth p95 fell from 120 -> 40, batcher_wait_ms median down to 90ms. Leaving throttled max_queue_depth in place for 15 minutes for stability.

sophia: Product/PM asks — can we make this visible in Console (token-level spans) so power users can detect metering auth pressure? Opening ticket: RH-1284.

raj: Created PR to decouple token refresh workers and add 429 short-circuit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7125

maria: Customer accepted workaround for now. Keeping thread open for postmortem and permanent fix ETA.

alex: Adding to incidents backlog; assign postmortem to raj+kevin. :white_check_mark:
